purpose: Teach: 亭主/眼差し/就く/むかっ/無くなり/申さ/ゆけ/沈み

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがしっかり亭主役を務められた
lines.en: You know, when he was younger, your father really knew how to lead.
lines.style: Soft, reaching backward in time. Voice settles into memory. Slow unhurried pace. Tender recognition mixed with the weight of years passed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お孫様への眼差しが優しかったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — and he had such a gentle way of looking at his grandchildren, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm affirmation. Voice brightens slightly on the memory. Intimate, turning toward him. A small lift at the end, inviting agreement rather than asking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが村長に就く決断をされた
lines.en: When he was young, he made the decision to become village headman.
lines.style: Quiet reverence for the weight of that choice. Pace deliberate, steady. The tone of someone marking an important threshold. Slight pause before 'headman'.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、神社にむかって毎日参られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he would pray at the shrine every single day for it, wouldn't he, dear?
lines.style: Knowing warmth. Voice carries the specificity of having witnessed this ritual. Gentle insistence — not questioning but confirming something sacred they both held.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは古い物が無くなりがちな時代を惜しまれた
lines.en: Back then, he mourned how the old ways were disappearing.
lines.style: Melancholy, but not bitter. Voice carries both his loss and his respect for what was fading. Measured, almost meditative. A pause where the sorrow lives.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、「申されます」と丁寧に言葉を選ばれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And the way he chose his words so carefully, so respectfully — you remember that, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Admiring recall. Voice lingers on the precision of his speech. Tender, almost protective of this memory. Turns to him as if asking him to help keep it real.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがゆけば皆が安心した
lines.en: When he would go out, everyone felt reassured.
lines.style: Simple certainty. Voice carries the weight of collective trust. Slow, almost solemnly. The phrase lands like a fact held in the body.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、夕日が沈み行く頃に縁側に座られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And at dusk, sitting there on the veranda, looking out — that's how I see him now, dear.
lines.style: Voice becomes softer, more distant. As if seeing him there again. Tender and a little fragile. Trailing off gently, like watching the sun sink. Intimate turn to him at the end.
